title: Anchored regression auditor for autotune decisioning
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Ship an anchored regression auditor that evaluates automated batching/caching recommendations and safe-config applies by producing a composite risk score and mapping that score to automated actions (approve, require human review, block/rollback). This auditor will be used in both offline autotune proposals and online canary workflows so that cost-driven config changes don’t cause quality regressions for customers.

Motivation and scope:
- Many autotune recommendations yield significant cost savings but occasionally produce semantic regressions (subtle hallucinations, degraded completion fidelity, or formatting breaks) that are hard to catch with single-metric checks.
- Current acceptance practices rely on ad-hoc golden prompts and small manual audits; we need an auditable, reproducible, and tunable system that scales across tenants and model variants.
- Scope: evaluator harness, anchored prompt set management, composite scoring, acceptance thresholds, CI-style statistical tests, rollout integration (shadow -> canary -> ramp), and a runbook for automated rollback triggers.

Design overview (high level):
1) Anchors: curated set of prompts that functions as coverage anchors rather than a single golden corpus. Anchors include: 1) stratified sampled real-traffic prompts (privacy-sanitized), 2) synthetic stress cases for known failure modes (formatting, code, lists), and 3) per-customer high-value anchors for top-account SLAs. Each anchor is tagged with an intent and baseline response fingerprint.

2) Multi-dimensional metrics: for each anchor we collect:
   - embedding cosine similarity to baseline response (semantic drift)
   - token delta and generation length changes (unexpected truncation/verbosity)
   - log-likelihood ratio (LLR) between baseline model outputs and candidate outputs (surrogate for confidence)
   - hallucination detector score (knowledge cutoff checks / fact-check heuristics)
   - structured field diff for models using structured output (schema violation rate)
   - downstream task metric where applicable (e.g., reranking NDCG / classification F1 computed on an anchor test set)

3) Composite risk score: metrics are normalized and combined into a single risk score using weighted sum with per-metric caps. We will allow per-customer weight overrides for high-sensitivity accounts. The initial weight presets are conservative (favoring recall of regressions).

4) Statistical acceptance rules: use a non-inferiority framework for continuous metrics. For each metric we compute a bootstrap 95% CI of the difference (candidate - baseline). Acceptance requires the CI upper bound to be within the predefined non-inferiority margin for semantic similarity and task metrics. For categorical/binary checks (schema violation), require absolute failure rate delta < margin and Fisher’s exact test p-value above threshold. We require at least 3 independent anchor strata to pass.

5) Action mapping: composite risk -> action mapping in initial rollout:
   - risk <= 0.2 => safe: shadow apply allowed, canary ramp allowed
   - 0.2 < risk <= 0.5 => manual review required: safety queue, engineering/PM signoff before canary
   - risk > 0.5 => block: do not approve apply; if already applied, auto-rollback trigger

6) Canary and rollback policy:
   - Shadow run for full candidate config across small fraction of traffic (internal only) with anchored scoring.
   - Canary ramp strategy: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% over fixed windows (24h per step), require metrics to remain within acceptance at each step.
   - Auto-rollback triggers: if composite risk delta exceeds 0.4 from baseline OR any critical anchor (per-customer anchor tagged critical) fails by > margin within the first 12 hours after canary, initiate automatic rollback and open incident.

Implementation tasks (this ticket):
- Dataset curation: build initial anchor set (global anchors + 10 per top-10 customers). Deliverable: anchors v1 CSV.
- Eval harness: implement evaluator that runs baseline vs candidate and computes the metric suite and bootstrap CIs. Unit tests + synthetic regression fuzz tests.
- Composite scorer: implement normalization, weighting presets, and config override hooks for customer sensitivity.
- Console integration: expose anchor-level diffs and composite risk on the Console rollout page; add an API endpoint for the auditor.
- Rollout wiring: plug auditor into existing config apply pipeline (shadow -> canary stages).
- Runbook and alerts: draft an automated rollback runbook and Slack PagerDuty play for on-call.

Acceptance criteria:
- Anchors v1 available and documented in Confluence with provenance for each item.
- Eval harness runs end-to-end in CI (unit + integration tests) and produces composite risk with deterministic outputs for seeded inputs.
- Console shows per-anchor diffs and composite risk for shadow and canary runs.
- Canary policy enforces acceptance thresholds and triggers manual-review or auto-rollback as specified.
- No customer outages in a 2-week internal pilot across staging tenants.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Larger anchor sets improve coverage but increase evaluation time and cost; mitigation: stratified anchors and early-stopping heuristics (stop when risk already above block threshold).
- False positives (spurious drift alerts) could block cost savings; mitigation: conservative initial weights and human-in-the-loop for mid-risk cases.
- Per-customer anchors increase privacy and operational overhead; mitigation: sanitize and allow opt-in customer anchor enrollment for SLAs.

Data / security considerations:
- All real-traffic anchors must be PII-sanitized before entering the corpus. Work with security/legal to sign off on the sanitization pipeline.
- Audit logs for every config apply and auditor decision must be persisted for compliance.
